   1|# Requirements Specification
   2|
   3|## 1. Project Overview
   4|
   5|**Project**: Python Command-Line Calculator
   6|
   7|**Description**: A command-line calculator application written in Python that supports basic arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division), operator precedence, parentheses, and error handling. Results are displayed with two decimal places.
   8|
   9|**Target Users**: End users who need to perform simple mathematical calculations via the command line.
  10|
  11|**Business Goals**:
  12|- Provide reliable arithmetic operation functionality
  13|- Ensure calculation accuracy
  14|- Provide clear error feedback
  15|
  16|---
  17|## 2. Domain Model
  18|
  19|### Expression
  20|- Description: A mathematical expression input by the user, consisting of numbers, operators, and parentheses.
  21|
  22|  Attributes:
  23|  - `raw_input` (`string`, required): The original input string from the user
  24|  - `parsed_tokens` (`list`, required): List of tokens after lexical analysis
  25|  - `result` (`float`, required): The computed result rounded to two decimal places
  26|
  27|  Relationships:
  28|### Error
  29|- Description: An error that occurs during input validation or computation.
  30|
  31|  Attributes:
  32|  - `type` (`string`, required): Type of error (e.g., division_by_zero, syntax_error, overflow)
  33|  - `message` (`string`, required): Human-readable error message
  34|
  35|  Relationships:
  36|
  37|---
  38|## 3. Actors
  39|
  40|### ACT-01: End User
  41|- Description: A user who interacts with the calculator via the command line to perform calculations.
  42|- Goals:
  43|  - Input a mathematical expression and receive the correct result
  44|  - Receive clear error messages for invalid input
  45|
  46|---
  47|## 4. Functional Requirements
  48|
  49|
  50|### FR-01 [CRITICAL] Basic Arithmetic Operations
  51|- **Description**: The calculator shall support addition (+), subtraction (-), multiplication (*), and division (/).
  52|- **Priority**: critical
  53|- **Actors**: ACT-01

  55|  **Acceptance Criteria**:
  56|  - [ ] AC1: Input '2+3' returns 5.00
  57|  - [ ] AC2: Input '5-2' returns 3.00
  58|  - [ ] AC3: Input '4*3' returns 12.00
  59|  - [ ] AC4: Input '10/4' returns 2.50
  60|
  61|### FR-02 [CRITICAL] Operator Precedence
  62|- **Description**: The calculator shall respect standard operator precedence: multiplication and division before addition and subtraction.
  63|- **Priority**: critical
  64|- **Actors**: ACT-01
  65|- **Dependencies**: FR-01
  66|
  67|  **Acceptance Criteria**:
  68|  - [ ] AC1: Input '2+3*4' returns 14.00
  69|  - [ ] AC2: Input '10-2*3' returns 4.00
  70|
  71|### FR-03 [HIGH] Parentheses Support
  72|- **Description**: The calculator shall support parentheses to override operator precedence.
  73|- **Priority**: high
  74|- **Actors**: ACT-01
  75|- **Dependencies**: FR-02
  76|
  77|  **Acceptance Criteria**:
  78|  - [ ] AC1: Input '(2+3)*4' returns 20.00
  79|  - [ ] AC2: Input '10/(2+3)' returns 2.00
  80|
  81|### FR-04 [HIGH] Result Formatting
  82|- **Description**: The calculator shall display results rounded to two decimal places.
  83|- **Priority**: high
  84|- **Actors**: ACT-01
  85|- **Dependencies**: FR-01
  86|
  87|  **Acceptance Criteria**:
  88|  - [ ] AC1: Input '1/3' returns 0.33
  89|  - [ ] AC2: Input '2' returns 2.00
  90|

  95|- **Dependencies**: FR-01

 140|## 5. Non-Functional Requirements
 141|
 142|
 143|### NFR-01: Response Time
 144|- Category: performance
 145|- Description: The calculator shall compute and display results within 1 second for typical expressions.
 146|- Target: Response time < 1 second for expressions up to 100 characters
 147|
 148|### NFR-02: Error Message Clarity
 149|- Category: usability
 150|- Description: Error messages shall be descriptive and indicate the nature of the error.
 151|- Target: All error messages must be in plain English and understandable by non-technical users
 152|
 153|### NFR-03: Accuracy
 154|- Category: reliability
 155|- Description: All calculations shall be accurate to within 0.01 of the true mathematical result, given the constraints of floating-point arithmetic.
 156|- Target: Results must match expected values when rounded to two decimal places
 157|
 158|### NFR-04: Code Modularity
 159|- Category: maintainability
 160|- Description: The code shall be organized into separate modules for tokenization, parsing, evaluation, and error handling.
 161|- Target: Each module shall have a single responsibility and be testable independently
 162|
 163|### NFR-05: Input Validation
 164|- Category: security
 165|- Description: All user input shall be validated to prevent expression injection or infinite loops.
 166|- Target: No input shall cause the application to crash or hang
 167|

 169|## 6. Use Cases

 171|
 172|### UC-01: Perform Basic Calculation
 173|- Actors: ACT-01
 174|
 175|  **Preconditions**:
 176|  - Calculator application is running and waiting for input
 177|
 178|  **Main Flow**:
 179|  1. 1. User enters a mathematical expression (e.g., '2+3')
 180|  2. 2. System tokenizes the input
 181|  3. 3. System parses tokens into an abstract syntax tree (AST) respecting operator precedence and parentheses
 182|  4. 4. System evaluates the AST
 183|  5. 5. System rounds the result to two decimal places
 184|  6. 6. System displays the result (e.g., '5.00')
 185|  7. 7. System prompts for next input
 186|
 187|  **Alternative Flows**:
 188|  - When If input is invalid (syntax error):
 189|    - 2a. System detects invalid syntax
 190|    - 3a. System displays error message
 191|    - 4a. System prompts for next input
 192|  - When If division by zero:
 193|    - 4b. System detects division by zero during evaluation
 194|    - 5b. System displays 'Error: Division by zero'
 195|    - 6b. System prompts for next input
 196|  - When If overflow occurs:
 197|    - 4c. System detects overflow
 198|    - 5c. System displays 'Error: Overflow'
 199|    - 6c. System prompts for next input
 200|
 201|  **Postconditions**:
 202|  - Result or error message is displayed
 203|  - Application is ready for next input
 204|
 205|  **Business Rules**:
 206|  - Operator precedence: * and / before + and -
 207|  - Parentheses override precedence
 208|  - Result rounded to two decimal places
 209|
 210|### UC-02: Exit Calculator
 211|- Actors: ACT-01
 212|
 213|  **Preconditions**:
 214|  - Calculator application is running and waiting for input
 215|
 216|  **Main Flow**:
 217|  1. 1. User enters 'exit' or 'quit'
 218|  2. 2. System terminates the application
 219|
 220|  **Postconditions**:
 221|  - Application is terminated
 222|
 223|---
 224|## 7. Constraints
 225|
 226|- **technical**: The application must be implemented in Python 3.6 or higher.
 227|- **technical**: No external libraries beyond the Python standard library may be used.
 228|- **business**: The application must be executable from the command line without any installation steps beyond having Python installed.
 229|
 230|---
 231|## 8. Risk Assessment
 232|
 233|| Risk | Probability | Impact | Mitigation | Contingency |
 234||------|-------------|--------|------------|-------------|
 235|| Division by zero error | medium | high | Implement explicit check for zero divisor before performing division. | Display user-friendly error message and continue. |
 236|| Floating-point precision issues | medium | medium | Use Python's Decimal module for precise arithmetic, or round results to two decimal places. | Accept minor rounding errors within tolerance. |
 237|| Numeric overflow | low | medium | Check for overflow by catching OverflowError or using limits. | Display overflow error message. |
 238|| User input format errors | high | medium | Implement robust input validation and tokenization. | Provide clear error messages and prompt again. |
 239|| Special characters in input | medium | medium | Whitelist allowed characters (digits, operators, parentheses, decimal point). | Reject input with invalid characters and show error. |
 240|| Code maintainability issues | low | medium | Use modular design with separate functions/classes for tokenization, parsing, evaluation, and error handling. | Refactor as needed. |
 241|| Insufficient test coverage | medium | high | Write unit tests for each module covering normal cases, edge cases, and error cases. | Add tests incrementally. |
 242|| Expression injection (e.g., using eval) | medium | high | Do not use eval(); implement a custom parser and evaluator. | Sanitize input thoroughly. |
 243|| Infinite loop due to malformed expression | low | high | Implement recursion limits or iterative parsing with bounded loops. | Set a maximum recursion depth and catch recursion errors. |
 244|
 245|---
 246|## 9. Assumptions
 247|
 248|- The user has Python 3.6 or higher installed.
 249|- The user runs the application from a command-line interface.
 250|- Input expressions are entered as a single line of text.
 251|- The calculator does not need to support functions (e.g., sin, cos) or variables.
 252|- The calculator uses standard floating-point arithmetic with rounding to two decimal places.
 253|- The application will not be used in a multi-user or networked environment.
